topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory welcome, lecturer background, and outlines the core learning outcomes for the lecture.

topics.label: Etiology of Cancer: Genetics, Chance, and Environmental Exposures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the conceptual framework of cancer causation, evaluating the interplay between intrinsic replication errors, inherited predispositions, and environmental exposures using global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious Agents and Pathogen-Driven Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious pathogens such as bacteria, parasites, and viruses contribute to malignant transformation, illustrated through the etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Carcinogenesis and Tumor Promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the cellular and biochemical mechanisms by which chemical and physical exposures cause cancer, including direct DNA damage, metabolic activation, tumor promotion via chronic inflammation, and developmental susceptibility windows.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the analytical and experimental strategies used to detect carcinogens and prove their carcinogenicity, including mutational signature analysis, population biobanks, animal models, and the Ames assay.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Analysis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture with a concluding reflection on evaluating carcinogen risks versus benefits and final concluding remarks.
